description: Canonical declared-count summary consumed by Verify-Complete-Hardening.ps1 and report consumers. Every value must reconcile with the corresponding module target inventory; changing a number alone is intentionally rejected by deterministic consistency checks.

framework.totalModes: Default-decision totals with Strict, the default Privacy mode (66 base targets including services, plus 27 Tier 1 policy-based in-box app-removal policy targets declared unconditionally: NotChecked when unselected on an eligible standalone client, NotApplicable when unsupported or externally managed). MSRecommended applies a smaller Privacy profile (framework total 658), Paranoid a larger one (711). verificationScope is the stable total that every complete verification reports: all seven modules with the complete 127-target Privacy inventory, where targets outside the selected Privacy profile are NotChecked by choice. Eleven visible interactive-user preference targets are included in every mode and remain separate from managed-policy effectiveness claims. App-removal effects are destructive and outside exact end-to-end BAVR: Tier 1 restores only its policy values exactly, and Tier 2 is a separate best-effort action. Tier 2 is not part of this count (see modules.Privacy.bloatwareBestEffortApps).

SecurityBaseline.note: Registry = 336 parsed Computer + User registry.pol entries of the Windows 11 v26H2 baseline (v2) minus the native WindowsFirewall PolicyVersion format entry; SecurityTemplate = 79 parsed minus 12 INF metadata entries (Unicode/Version); AuditPolicies = 23 subcategories. All real security directives remain in the applied plan.

ASR.note: Nineteen declared Defender ASR identities. On Windows 11 clients, 18 are applicable (16 Block-by-default and 2 user-configurable); Microsoft's operating-system matrix marks the Exchange-server Webshell rule NotApplicable.

DNS.note: Five exact aggregates: primary IPv4, secondary IPv4, the IPv6 pair in every binding-enabled adapter's native/registry state (plus effective DNS-client readback while IPv6 transport is enabled), all four selected-provider DoH registrations, and DoHPolicy/fallback consistency including Microsoft DNS_INTERFACE_SETTINGS3 per-adapter-family DoH properties. The native interface properties make the persisted encrypted configuration visible as encrypted in Windows Settings without adding a second UX decision. Schema-6 BAVR seals effective resolver scope and native/UI-visible DoH scope separately, plus the raw registry values Windows' DoH APIs cannot reproduce, and restores all exact prior states; when DisabledComponents=0xFF disables IPv6 transport, the label is not a claim of active IPv6 traffic.

Privacy.note: MSRecommended base = 43 mode-specific registry targets plus 4 OneDrive/Store targets; choosing Preserve for Cloud Clipboard reduces that active base by one. Eleven base targets are visible interactive-user preferences and do not inherit managed-policy effectiveness claims; two of them are the cloud content search toggles that Windows sets from AllowCloudSearch=0 and keeps after that policy is removed, so they are owned for exact restore, two are the account-notification preferences in Settings and Start, and one is the advertising-ID switch, which turns the ID off on Home, where the AdvertisingInfo policy is unavailable. Every mode also writes the three values behind Recommendations and offers in Settings, which Windows writes itself when that switch is turned off, sets AcceptedPrivacyPolicy=0 so the inking and typing switch shows the state its collection values enforce, and selects the Search location and Search highlights policies (Pro and higher). Strict/Paranoid disable periodic Windows settings/app-list cloud backup and block cellular text-message cloud sync. Paranoid alone denies app access to presence sensing, the eye tracker and motion data, and disables local device-search history, online font providers, automatic device-metadata companion-app downloads and Windows Error Reporting (by policy on Pro and higher and with Microsoft's documented WER setting on Home, each NotApplicable on the other editions; WerSvc is set to its Windows default, Manual). MSRecommended/Strict preserve useful local search ranking while all modes disable their selected web/Bing surfaces. Strict, the default since 2.3.0, declares 66 base targets including services, so registry and total describe Strict; Paranoid base declares 100 including services/tasks. All modes additionally declare the same 27 Tier 1 policy identities. The Paranoid inventory contains every MSRecommended and Strict target identity; verification always evaluates these 127 targets and reports targets outside the selected profile as NotChecked by choice. HKCU targets belong only to the interactive Explorer owner; offline profiles remain untouched. Schema-7 BAVR seals decisions, management/applicability, Applied, NotChecked and NotApplicable inventories. Tier 1 = root Enabled, an empty root DynamicRemovalList REG_MULTI_SZ, and 25 static Package-Family-Name RemovePackage flags, exactly matching the current inbox gpedit layout; four static flags are selected by the NoID Privacy curated opt-in (News, Weather, Xbox and Microsoft Copilot). Policy-value prestate restores exactly, but downstream app/data removal does not. Tier 1 is NotChecked when unselected on eligible standalone Enterprise/Education 24H2+, NotApplicable when unsupported, multi-session, AD-domain joined or MDM registered, and NotChecked (cannot verify) when management state cannot be proven. A management query that still fails after three attempts is treated like a managed PC: every Privacy policy path, service and scheduled task stays unchanged and is reported NotChecked (cannot verify), while ordinary non-policy user preferences remain selectable. On Home, the Windows policies measured as honoured there (diagnostic data, app permissions, clipboard, nearby sharing, location, Find my device, settings sync, tailored experiences, cloud search) apply as on Pro; every other Windows policy target is NotApplicable on Home. Tier 2 = 18 base per-user AppX candidates including Microsoft Copilot plus the separately selected Weather/Widgets package, each with a catalog-bound sealed inventory; both choices are valid verification outcomes. Tier 2 is excluded from totalSettings because Store reinstall cannot reproduce exact app data/package/provisioning state and is a separate original-user-only best-effort action.

AntiAI.note: 50 config-derived registry targets across 11 registry groups plus one URI-handler group; two are the per-user start-at-sign-in settings of the Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot apps, written only when the app is registered for that user, and the Edge Update Copilot install block is written only on domain-joined or MDM-enrolled devices because Edge Update ignores its policies elsewhere. User-scope values target the interactive desktop user's loaded HKEY_USERS hive, not the elevated account's HKCU. Complete verification includes four real source hives for absence of the two Copilot URI handlers. Preview/edition/product applicability is reported separately from registry/source-state exactness.

EdgeHardening.note: Exact Edge scope: 24 Microsoft v151 baseline values plus nine separately labelled, currently documented NoID Privacy additions; two of them keep Edge from starting at sign-in and from running in the background after its last window closes (StartupBoostEnabled=0, BackgroundModeEnabled=0). The LGPO **delvals. row is metadata, not a policy. Default does not select the block-all extension value (32 selected); strict selects all 33. DynamicCodeSettings is written as Edge's default 0 so Edge can print; the baseline value 1 is a separate opt-in choice (allowBrowserDynamicCode=false) and does not change the count. Four SmartScreen values and BrowserCodeIntegritySetting are applied only after AD-domain or eligible Pro/Enterprise MDM registration proof; otherwise they remain untouched and are NotApplicable. Documented policies above an installed Edge version are staged for a future update; registry verification is not presented as proof that the older browser consumed them.

AdvancedSecurity.note: Maximum declared verification scope after expanding aggregates: 17 deterministic firewall targets (16 stable module-owned rules plus Shields Up) and 31 non-firewall registry/service/adapter/API targets. WPAD contributes exactly two checks: Microsoft's documented WinHTTP DisableWpad machine value and the interactive Explorer user's WinINet PROXY_TYPE_AUTO_DETECT bit, changed and restored through the documented API while preserving every unrelated proxy flag; the user check is NotApplicable when no interactive Explorer user exists. Optional profile choices remain NotChecked when not selected; an explicit firewall-layer skip reports applicable firewall targets as NotChecked and never as Applied/Passed. On Home, 13 RDP-host, WirelessDisplay and optional-content Windows Update policy targets are NotApplicable rather than written or passed; the Delivery Optimization policy applies on every edition because Windows 11 Home was measured to honour it. Windows Update keeps optional non-security updates user-selected (WindowsUpdate.admx AllowOptionalContent: SetAllowOptionalContent=1 with AllowOptionalContent=3), disables the early-rollout UX preference, preserves Microsoft-product update enrollment, and disables P2P delivery. The obsolete WDigest policy removed by Microsoft's Windows 11 25H2 baseline and Windows PowerShell 2.0 removed from updated 24H2 images in August 2025 are not written or counted. The historical PowerShellV2 reader recognizes older sealed artifacts for BAVR compatibility, restores only while Windows still exposes the recorded feature identity and otherwise names the removed component in a warning while the rest of the session is restored; new runs do not query, back up, apply, verify or report the removed component. The legacy SRP path rules (eight values) and the five Wireless Display Connect values that Windows reads only through MDM are no longer written or counted; schema-5 sessions saved by earlier builds still restore them.
